summary: Hawking's calculation says a black hole evaporates into featureless heat, destroying information. Quantum mechanics says information cannot be destroyed. This is the black hole information puzzle.

If evaporation is ordinary quantum evolution, the entropy of the radiation must rise and then fall back to zero, following the Page curve. In 2019 the falling part was derived from gravity itself, using quantum extremal surfaces.
The answer has an error-correction meaning: after the Page time, part of the black hole's interior, the island, is encoded in the radiation that has already escaped.

glossary.def: The thermal glow by which a black hole slowly loses mass.
Quantum evolution that never destroys information: pure states stay pure.
The entropy of the radiation over time if evaporation is unitary: up, then down to zero.
The moment the radiation's entropy turns over, roughly halfway through evaporation.
A region inside the black hole that belongs to the entanglement wedge of the radiation.
The surface that extremises area/4G plus bulk entropy; the edge of the island.
The argument that an old black hole returns information thrown into it almost immediately.

keyPoints: Hawking: radiation entropy keeps rising; unitarity: it must return to zero.
Page curve: S(radiation) follows min(radiation so far, black hole remaining).
Island formula: S(R) = min over islands of [Area(∂I)/4G + S_bulk(R ∪ I)].
Before the Page time: no island. After: an island appears and the entropy falls.
After the Page time the interior is encoded in the radiation, in a highly scrambled, error-corrected way.

items: Quick recap of the last chapter, The bridge to deep learning:
• Depth in a network, steps of RG and radial depth in AdS all organise information by scale.
• Random tensor network entropies = free energy of an Ising model = a Boltzmann machine.
• EFL: fit the couplings to entanglement data; the learned graph is the bulk geometry.
• Critical data in, hyperbolic geometry out; gapped data gives a shallow network.
• AdS/DL: radial slices = layers, metric = weights, boundary data = training set.

ELI5. Imagine burning a diary. The smoke and ash look like a mess, but in principle every word is still in there, scrambled. A black hole that slowly evaporates is like a very slow fire. The question is whether the words really are in the smoke.

Now the real words. Hawking's calculation says the radiation's entropy rises forever, which would destroy information. Quantum mechanics requires the Page curve: up until the Page time, then down to zero.

In 2019 this was derived from gravity with the island formula. After the Page time a region inside the black hole, the island, belongs to the radiation's entanglement wedge, so the interior is encoded in the radiation like an error-correcting code.
Try it. In the lab, slide to 6 of 12 qubits to find the Page time, then see how soon after it the diary becomes readable.
If you remember one thing: the entropy goes up, turns at the Page time and comes back down, and the inside is encoded in what came out.

In 1974 Hawking showed that black holes are not completely black. Quantum effects make them glow, lose mass, and eventually evaporate. The glow is thermal: it seems to depend only on the black hole's mass, charge and spin, not on what fell in.

That is a problem. Make a black hole from a pure quantum state, say a carefully prepared star. Let it evaporate completely. If what is left is purely thermal radiation, a pure state has become a mixed one, and information has been destroyed.

Quantum mechanics forbids exactly that: its evolution is unitary. Hawking's 1976 conclusion was that gravity breaks quantum mechanics. AdS/CFT says otherwise: the black hole is a state of an ordinary quantum theory on the boundary, and that theory is unitary. So information must come out. But how?
Don Page sharpened the question in 1993 by tracking one number: the entanglement entropy of the radiation. Early on, each emitted particle is entangled with the black hole, so the entropy rises.
But the radiation can never be more entangled with the black hole than the black hole's own entropy allows, and that is shrinking. (See Figure 12.1 below.)

lesson.caption: Figure 12.1. Hawking's rising entropy against the Page curve required by unitarity.

items: The turning point is the Page time, when the black hole has lost about half its entropy. After it, the entropy of the radiation must fall, reaching zero when the hole is gone and the radiation alone is in a pure state. Hawking's calculation gives the rising line forever.
For decades nobody could get the turn-over from gravity.

You can see the Page curve in a quantum system you can simulate. Take a random pure state of $n$ qubits, a stand-in for a thoroughly scrambled black hole, and call the first $k$ qubits 'radiation'. Their entropy is very nearly $\min(k,\, n-k)$ bits. You will measure exactly this in the lab.

The breakthrough came in 2019, from Penington and from Almheiri, Engelhardt, Marolf and Maxfield. They applied the quantum extremal surface rule of chapter 7 to the radiation. The rule says: do not just take the obvious surface.
Consider every candidate, including surprising ones, extremise area plus bulk entropy, and take the smallest.
$R$ is the radiation far away and $I$ is a possible 'island': a region somewhere else, which you are allowed to include with the radiation at the price of its boundary area.

Early on, the best choice is no island at all, and the formula gives Hawking's rising answer. After the Page time a different choice wins: an island covering most of the black hole interior. (See Figure 12.2 below.)

lesson.caption: Figure 12.2. After the Page time the island, a region inside the black hole, belongs to the radiation.

items: Why does an island help? The interior partners of the Hawking particles lie in the island. Counting them together with the radiation removes their entanglement from the bulk entropy term. What is left is the area term, roughly the black hole's remaining entropy, which decreases.
The minimum of the two candidates is the Page curve. (See Table 12.1 below.)

lesson.title: Table 12.1. Two candidates for the radiation's entropy
head: No island
With an island
rows: about the horizon area/4G: the remaining black hole entropy
large and growing: all the Hawking pairs are split

items: Now connect this to chapter 10. The entanglement wedge of a region is what that region can reconstruct. After the Page time the entanglement wedge of the radiation includes the island.

So operators inside the black hole can, in principle, be reconstructed from the radiation alone. The interior is encoded in the Hawking radiation, as the bulk is encoded in the boundary: scrambled, spread out, and error-corrected.

Hayden and Preskill anticipated this in 2007. Throw a diary into an old black hole, one past its Page time. Because the hole is maximally entangled with the earlier radiation and scrambles quickly, the diary's information reappears in the radiation after only a few more particles are emitted.
Old black holes are information mirrors. In the lab you will watch the diary become readable just after the halfway point. (See Table 12.2 below.)

lesson.title: Table 12.2. Three eras of an evaporating black hole
head: Era
Entropy of radiation
Entanglement wedge of radiation
A diary thrown in
rows: stays hidden until the Page time
comes out almost at once, scrambled

items: What is and is not settled? The entropy curve is now derived from gravity, including from a careful sum over geometries called replica wormholes.
What is still being worked out is the detailed mechanism: exactly how the information is carried by the radiation, and what an observer falling in experiences.

Decoding the radiation in practice appears to be exponentially hard, which may be what protects the smooth interior. The puzzle has turned from 'is information lost?' into 'how is it encoded?', and the language of the answer is quantum error correction.
Memory trick: Up, Page, down; no island, then island. Radiation entropy goes Up, turns at the Page time, comes Down; no island before, island after.

summary: Every chapter has described the same object from a different side. Geometry, entanglement, error correction and layered networks are four views of how a boundary quantum system encodes a bulk world.
This chapter lines the views up, says what is established and what is still conjecture, and points to open problems.

The final lab lets you hold all four views at once in a single toy universe: measure entanglement with minimal cuts, read bulk points from boundary regions, train the geometry from data, and add a black hole.

The discrete Ryu-Takayanagi surface of a network.

How much hardware you can lose before logical information is gone; grows with bulk depth.
A simplified model that keeps the mechanism and drops the rest.
Open attempts to extend holography to universes like ours.

keyPoints: Geometry ↔ entanglement: RT, S = Area/4G.
Entanglement ↔ code: the entanglement wedge is what a region can correct for.
Code ↔ network: tensor networks are explicit holographic codes.
Network ↔ geometry: depth is scale (RG), and the weights can be learned from data.
Open: dynamics, time, and universes that are not AdS.

items: Quick recap of the last chapter, Black hole information: the Page curve and islands:
• Hawking: radiation entropy keeps rising; unitarity: it must return to zero.
• Page curve: S(radiation) follows min(radiation so far, black hole remaining).
• Island formula: S(R) = min over islands of [Area(∂I)/4G + S_bulk(R ∪ I)].
• Before the Page time: no island. After: an island appears and the entropy falls.
• After the Page time the interior is encoded in the radiation, in a highly scrambled, error-corrected way.

ELI5. Imagine four people describing an elephant in the dark. One feels the shape, one feels how the parts are joined, one notices that it still works if a bit is hidden, and one notices it is built in layers. They are all describing one animal.
Now the real words. Geometry, entanglement, error correction and layered networks are four descriptions of how a boundary quantum system encodes a bulk world.

Minimal surfaces are entropies; a region's entanglement wedge is what it can reconstruct; tensor networks are explicit codes; and network depth is scale, with weights that can be learned. Open questions remain about time, black hole interiors and universes that are not AdS.
Try it. In the final lab, do all four in one toy universe: cut it, read it, train it, and put a black hole in it.
If you remember one thing: one object, four views: geometry, entanglement, code, network.
Step back. You have met one idea in four languages. (See Figure 13.1 below.)

lesson.caption: Figure 13.1. Four views of one holographic state, and the results that connect them.

items: Geometry. The bulk is a curved space, AdS, whose depth coordinate is the energy scale of the boundary theory. Black holes are hot states; horizons are entropy.
Entanglement. Areas of minimal surfaces are entanglement entropies (Ryu-Takayanagi). Reduce the entanglement and the space comes apart. Two entangled systems can share a wormhole.

Code. The bulk is logical information stored redundantly in the boundary hardware. A boundary region can read exactly its entanglement wedge. Deep points are the best protected. The area term in RT is part of the code's own structure.

Network. Coarse-graining builds a layered network whose shape is the geometry and whose cuts are the surfaces. Its bond strengths are weights that can be learned from entanglement data by gradient descent, just as a neural network is trained. (See Table 13.1 below.)

items: One more link deserves a sentence, since it closes the circle. If the RT formula holds for every region, and the boundary entanglement obeys a quantum-information identity called the first law of entanglement, then the bulk geometry must satisfy Einstein's equations, at least for small changes around empty AdS (Faulkner, Guica, Hartman, Myers and Van Raamsdonk, 2013).
Gravity's equation itself can be read as a statement about entanglement.
A short history helps to see how the pieces arrived. (See Figure 13.2 below.) (See Table 13.2 below.)

lesson.caption: Figure 13.2. Fifty years of ideas, from black hole entropy to islands.

rows: established within semiclassical gravity; counted microscopically for many string theory black holes

well established as the structure of bulk reconstruction; exact only approximately
toy models: they capture the mechanism, not the full theory
working algorithms and strong analogies; an active research area
derived for the entropy; the detailed mechanism is under study

items: The biggest open questions. First, time: tensor networks and codes describe one moment; gravity is about how geometry changes. Second, the interior of black holes and the experience of someone falling in. Third, our universe is not AdS.

It is expanding, closer to de Sitter space, and it is not known whether, or how, it has a holographic description. Fourth, locality: why does the bulk look local on scales much smaller than the AdS radius? Each of these is a research field.

Now the final lab. It uses one toy universe, the layered network of chapters 9 and 11, and asks you to look at it in all four ways. In level 1 you measure entanglement with minimal cuts, and check that a region and its complement agree: geometry from entanglement.

In level 2 you choose bulk points and find which boundary regions can read them, discovering that the centre is readable from many different regions and that shallow points are easily lost: the bulk as a code.

In level 3 the bonds start out wrong and you train them from entanglement data by gradient descent: the geometry is learned. In level 4 you heat the system and a horizon appears: region and complement stop agreeing, the whole boundary has entropy, and points behind the horizon cannot be read.

items: Where to go next. For a careful first course, the open notes at adscft.org cover the foundations and then bulk reconstruction, error correction and black hole information.
Daniel Harlow's lecture notes on black holes and quantum information, and on the emergence of bulk physics, are the standard introductions to chapters 10 and 12.

For the learning bridge, start with the Perimeter talk by Yi-Zhuang You and the papers behind it. And keep the toy universe in mind: when a statement about holography seems abstract, ask what it says about cuts, wedges and weights in the network. It almost always says something you can count.

sandbox.intro: A scripted lookup, not a calculator. Try: entropy, disk, ads, cft, branes, dictionary, rt, btz, hp, tfd, network, code, wedge, learn, page, island, help

out: entropy    S = A / 4G  (Bekenstein-Hawking)
disk       Poincare disk: ds^2 = 4(dx^2+dy^2)/(1-r^2)^2
ads        Poincare AdS: ds^2 = (L^2/z^2)(-dt^2 + dx^2 + dz^2), boundar
cft        scale invariant quantum field theory
branes     N D3-branes: SU(N) N=4 super Yang-Mills  =  strings on AdS5
dictionary Z_CFT[phi0] = Z_gravity[phi -> phi0]
rt         S(A) = Area(gamma_A)/4G, gamma_A the minimal surface anchore
btz        ds^2 = -(r^2-rh^2)/L^2 dt^2 + L^2 dr^2/(r^2-rh^2) + r^2 dphi
hp         Hawking-Page: thermal AdS below T = 1/(2 pi L), black hole a
tfd        |TFD> = sum_n e^(-beta E_n/2) |n>_L |n>_R / sqrt(Z)
network    S(A) <= bonds cut x log chi
code       three qutrits: |0~> = (|000>+|111>+|222>)/sqrt3 ...
wedge      entanglement wedge of A: bulk between A and its RT surface
learn      gradient descent: w <- w - eta dL/dw
page       S(radiation) ~ min(radiated, black hole left)
island     S(R) = min ext [ Area(dI)/4G + S_bulk(R u I) ]
